# Home

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/>

AI Enablement & Implementation · Private Equity

## AI implementation for firms where judgment is the product.

We train entire investment teams on AI, then build AI systems on the workflows that matter.

The technology underneath this work changes weekly: new models, new tools, shifting best practice. Most firms train once and fall behind quietly. Solven's programmes are monthly because the frontier is weekly: your team, analyst to partner, stays current as the market moves.

Enablement

#### Learn the tools, at every level of the firm.

Hands-on Claude sessions for the whole team, from the newest analyst to the managing partner. A four-session arc from first principles to building with the most advanced tools in the suite.

Build

#### Then build AI systems on your workflows.

Agents, automation, and workflow systems applied to the real work: contract redlining, IC memo interrogation, portfolio reporting. Build hours pair with the training so confidence becomes real systems.

AI Diligence

#### And tell real AI from marketing jargon.

Independent diligence for funds: we pressure-test whether a target or a pitching founder is genuinely AI-native, or simply fluent in the vocabulary, before the term sheet is signed.

Token Economics

#### And make every token earn its place.

Where your compute spend actually goes, what it returns, and how to pace it, so the firm's token budget lasts the full year, not the first quarter.

### Four practices, four entry points into the firm.

Each maps to a different seat at the table, and each is designed to sharpen judgment rather than substitute for it.

#### Diligence & deal flow

First-pass diligence, question banks, comparables, data room synthesis, and sourcing screens, all defensible at investment committee.

#### Portfolio operations

Board packs, quarterly reports, KPI monitoring, and variance flagging that scale with the portfolio, not the headcount.

#### Investor relations & compliance

LP letters, capital call narratives, and SFDR / CSRD / ESG workflows, at the cadence investors expect and with the audit trail intact.

#### Knowledge & methodology

Institutional memory, workflow playbooks, and analyst training in the AI-as-adversary methodology that holds under pressure.

AI Diligence

### Find out whether the AI is real.

When a target or a founder claims to be “AI-powered,” we give the fund a defensible read on what is genuine capability and what is marketing jargon, before the term sheet.

The pitch

- “Proprietary AI engine.”

- “AI-native from day one.”

- “Our models are the moat.”

- “The workflow is fully automated.”

What we surface

- The stack behind the story: built in-house, or a thin wrapper on a model anyone can rent.

- Whether the data and models are genuinely defensible, or commodity dressed up as a moat.

- Whether the team can ship what they claim, at the velocity they claim.

- Where AI actually touches the P&L, and where it is theatre for the raise.

The deliverable: a clear read for the investment committee covering what is real, what is veneer, and what it changes about the price.

Token Economics

### Make every token earn its place.

An unmanaged compute budget has a way of being gone by March. We show you where the tokens went, what they returned, and how to make the year's budget last the year.

#### Usage analytics

A clear read on where tokens go, by team, workflow, model, and prompt, so the spend that was invisible becomes legible.

#### ROI analytics

What each token actually returns. Cost measured per outcome, not per call, so you can see which workflows earn their keep and which don't.

#### Efficiency

Right-sized models, prompt caching, and tighter context: the same output for a fraction of the spend, without dropping quality.

#### Budget pacing

Forecasts and guardrails that keep consumption tracking the year, so there are no surprises and no scramble in the fourth quarter.

The deliverable: a token P&L the partners can read, showing what each workflow costs, what it earns, and the changes that stretch the same budget across the whole year.

The currency argument

### The frontier moves weekly. We keep your team on it.

A firm that trained its team six months ago is already operating on stale knowledge.

New models, new tools, new capabilities, shifting best practice: the ground under this work shifts on a weekly cadence. Our programmes are monthly precisely because the technology is weekly. Every person in the firm stays fluent with the frontier as it moves, without anyone having to track the firehose themselves.

Where we work

Built for private equity, real estate, and venture firms, from Lisbon to London.

Member of the Anthropic Partner Network · Phase 1

### Let's tune a programme to your firm's priorities.

A short conversation is the fastest way to see where Claude belongs in your team's work, and where it shouldn't.

The first thirty minutes are on us. So is the straight answer.

# Programmes

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/programmes>

Enablement · The programmes

## Genuine AI fluency at every level of the firm, from analyst to partner.

Hands-on Claude sessions that take an entire firm from first principles to building with the most advanced tools in the suite.

A team trained once is a team falling behind. The technology underneath this work shifts on a weekly cadence, so a firm that trained six months ago is already operating on stale knowledge.

Our programmes are monthly precisely because the technology is weekly. Each person learns to recognise where Claude belongs in their own work, and stays current as the market keeps moving.

Always on the frontier

### The frontier moves weekly. We keep your team on it.

New models, tools, and capabilities arrive on a weekly cadence. Our sessions land at a steady rhythm so the team is never more than one step behind the edge.

How it works

### On your own workflows, not generic demonstrations.

- i Hands-on, on the real work.Sessions run on the firm's actual deals, models, memos, and reports, so each person leaves knowing where Claude fits their day.

- ii Month one is breadth.Orientation across the full Claude ecosystem, from first principles to building, so the whole team shares a map of what is possible.

- iii From month two, we go deep.Later sessions concentrate on the areas the team finds most valuable. The session's arc stays; the path adapts.

- iv Trainers read the room.The topics below are guidance, not a script. Pace and emphasis follow the people in the room, analyst to partner.

What we cover

### The full Claude toolkit.

Each person learns which tool fits which part of their work, so the whole suite is in play, not just the chat box.

#### Claude.ai

Research, drafting, and analysis in the browser, with Projects, files, and web search in one place.

#### Claude Code

The most capable tool in the suite, and far more than a developer tool: organising files, automating recurring work, building real systems.

#### Claude for Chrome

Claude working alongside the pages and tools your team already uses, without leaving the browser.

#### Claude Cowork

Claude that takes actions across the desktop, running a workflow end to end rather than only generating text.

#### Claude for Excel

Formula generation and audit, data cleaning, and model building, with Claude reasoning across the whole workbook.

#### Claude for PowerPoint

Decks, charts, and IC-ready memos drawn from outlines, notes, or source documents, aligned to the house format.

### The four-session arc.

From how a model actually thinks, through conversation and production, to building agentic systems with Claude Code.

Session one · Foundations

#### How AI thinks.

Understand what a model is doing well enough to know when to trust it, and when to push back.

- The history of AI through the transformer breakthrough

- Tokens, embeddings, vectors, and attention

- How generation works: probability, sampling, run-to-run variance

- Where Claude is sharpest, where it fails, and why hallucinations happen

- The analyst-first principle and the habit of verification

How a model turns text into output

Session two · Conversation

#### Claude.ai.

The prompting craft that separates competent output from compelling, and the devil's advocate pattern at its core.

- The interface: chat, Projects, Memory, files, web search, Artifacts

- Structured prompting: XML tagging, role framing, output specs

- Few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought, and metaprompting

- The devil's advocate pattern: Claude as critic, not author

- Context-window management, token economics, knowing when to stop

Anatomy of a structured prompt

Session three · Production

#### Claude in the tools you already use.

Where the team's deliverables actually live: the workbook, the deck, and across the desktop.

- Claude for Excel: formula generation, audit trails, financial models, cross-sheet reasoning

- Claude for PowerPoint: decks from outlines, brand-aligning, IC-ready memos

- Claude Cowork: desktop automation and multi-app workflows

- The bigger idea: tools and function calling

- Why Claude + tools is fundamentally more capable than Claude alone

Tools around the model

Session four · Construction

#### Building with Claude Code.

The most capable tool in the suite, far beyond a developer tool: where AI-native workflows compound month over month.

- The agentic loop, version-controlled prompts, and markdown fluency

- Skills & SKILL.md: packaging team expertise as deployable capability

- MCP: connecting Claude to databases, APIs, and internal systems

- The infinite-horizon problem and explicit done-conditions

- Automation patterns: structured extraction, batch processing, report generation

The agentic loop

The thread

### Every session carries the analyst-first principle.

Analysts produce the formative work first, then bring Claude in as a critic, a red-teamer, and a verifier.

The risk in any rollout is that talented people become editors of drafts they cannot fully defend. We design every session the other way round. Verification habits, the devil's advocate pattern, AI as critic rather than author: the same skills that unconstrained use erodes are the ones we build.

That is what we mean by augmentation without cognitive atrophy, and it runs through all four sessions and everything that follows them.

Programme structure

### Built to flex around the firm.

#### Month to month

Programmes run monthly with no minimum commitment. Stay as long as the frontier keeps moving, which is to say, as long as it is useful.

#### Sessions plus build hours

Training pairs with optional build and consulting hours, so confidence from the room turns into real systems on real workflows.

#### On site or remote

Delivered at your office in Lisbon, remotely, or a mix. The format follows the team, not the other way round.

#### Open to the whole firm

Analyst to managing partner. Fluency is a firm-wide capability, not a specialism held by a few. Each engagement is scoped and priced bespoke.

### Questions firms ask before they book.

Straight answers to the questions that usually precede the first call. Anything unanswered here is a good opening for the call itself.

**Q: How is an engagement priced?**

Each engagement is scoped and priced individually: a six-person deal team and a forty-person firm are not the same programme. Programmes run monthly with no minimum commitment, so the decision you are making is a month's decision, not a year's.

**Q: How much of the team's time does the programme take?**

Month one is four sessions covering the full arc, from how a model thinks through to building with Claude Code. From month two the cadence is monthly, going deep on the areas the team finds most valuable. Sessions run on your own deals, models, and memos, so the time is spent on the actual work rather than beside it.

**Q: What happens to our firm's data during the sessions?**

Sessions run on your actual deals, models, and memos, so this question deserves a precise answer rather than a reassuring one. Data handling is settled during scoping, before any material is opened: whose accounts the work passes through, on what terms, and what, if anything, is retained afterwards. The answers are put in writing before the first session.

**Q: Which AI tools do you train on, and are we locking ourselves into one vendor?**

We train on the Claude suite: Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude in Excel, PowerPoint, Chrome, and Cowork. Solven is a member of the Anthropic Partner Network. That is a deliberate position, not an accident. On lock-in: session one teaches how any large model works, from tokens, attention, and probability to where hallucinations come from, and the verification habits we build are model-agnostic. If the market shifts, the fluency travels with your team.

**Q: Are the sessions delivered in Portuguese or English?**

Either, or both. We are based in Lisbon and work with firms from Lisbon to London, so sessions run in the language the room prefers. Written materials are in English, because the tools and the frontier are.

**Q: How do we know the programme worked?**

Three ways the firm can see rather than take on trust. The work itself: output that is defensible at investment committee, with the human contribution legible to senior reviewers. The token P&L from our token economics work: what each workflow costs and what it returns, in a form the partners can read. And the calibration reviews built into the methodology, which surface drift before it compounds.

**Q: Why Solven rather than a large consultancy, or doing this in-house?**

Three honest reasons. The work is specific: we do one thing, for investment firms, and sessions run on your deals and memos rather than a generic curriculum. The cadence is the product: the technology shifts weekly, and a one-off training project, internal or external, is stale within a quarter; our engagement is monthly because the frontier is. And the thesis is different: most enablement measures adoption; we design against cognitive offloading, so judgment gets sharper rather than thinner. If what a firm mainly needs is change management across a thousand seats, a large consultancy is the right call, and we will say so.

**Q: What happens after the programme ends?**

The engagement is monthly with no minimum commitment, so ending is a decision you can make any month. What the firm keeps: the verification habits; the prompts and skills built in session four, version-controlled files that live in your systems; and anything produced in build hours. Nothing is designed to make leaving hard.

**Q: Will this make our analysts dependent on AI?**

That risk is the reason the firm exists. The failure mode in most rollouts is not adoption failure; it is analysts becoming editors of drafts they cannot defend. Every session is built the other way round: the analyst produces a defensible first pass, then brings Claude in as a critic, a red-teamer, and a verifier. Used this way, the model sharpens exactly the skills that unconstrained use erodes. We call it augmentation without cognitive atrophy.

**Q: Can partners attend, or is this for analysts?**

The whole firm, analyst to managing partner. Fluency is a firm-wide capability, not a specialism held by a few, and each session is paced to the people in the room. The partners' sessions matter most: senior-led review is how the verification discipline holds.

Member of the Anthropic Partner Network · Phase 1

### A conversation to tune the programme to your firm's priorities.

Tell us where your team is today and what the next quarter looks like. We will shape the arc around it.

# Approach

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/approach>

The approach

## Augmentation without cognitive atrophy.

The risk in enterprise AI is not adoption failure. It is what happens to analytical judgment when adoption succeeds.

The risk

### Cognitive offloading.

When an analyst can produce a polished draft in a single prompt, the formative work quietly stops happening: sitting with the data, building a position from first principles, defending a number under pressure.

The analyst becomes a passive editor of model output. Quality looks the same on the page; the underlying judgment thins out. This is the failure mode a serious firm should be designing against.

The risk in any AI rollout is that talented people become editors of drafts they cannot fully defend.

The principle

### AI as adversary, not author.

We treat the model as a stress-tester of the analyst's reasoning, not a generator of it. The analyst forms a position first; the model challenges it. The analyst defends the work; the model probes for weakness.

Used this way, AI sharpens the very skills that unconstrained use erodes. The output is better and the judgment behind it is stronger, not weaker.

Analysts produce the formative work first, then bring Claude in as a critic, a red-teamer, and a verifier.

The practice

### Constraints that hold under pressure.

The principle becomes real through how the work is sequenced and reviewed. The shape varies by firm; the discipline does not.

- Analyst-firstThe analyst produces a defensible first pass before engaging the model.

- Show-your-workAppendices make the human contribution legible to senior reviewers.

- VerificationThe devil's advocate pattern is built into the workflow, not bolted on.

- CalibrationSenior-led reviews surface drift before it compounds across the team.

One thesis, both sides of the work

### The approach governs how we train and what we build.

It is not a slide at the front of a deck. It is the operating principle behind every session we teach and every system we ship.

#### How we train

Every session is designed the adversary-first way, so the team builds verification habits as it builds fluency.

#### What we build

Agents and workflows are designed to challenge and verify human reasoning, never to quietly replace it.

See it in practice

### The programmes put the principle to work.

The four-session arc carries the analyst-first principle from first principles through to building with Claude Code.

# Work

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/work>

Selected work

## Enablement and build, on real workflows.

A look at how the two sides of the work fit together on the workflows that fill an investment team's week.

Described by the work itself, by workflow and structure, with no metrics we cannot stand behind.

Capability 01

Diligence · financing · investment committee

### Firm-wide enablement, plus agents on the heaviest reviews.

#### Context

Diligence, financing, and investment-committee workflows are repetitive and judgment-heavy: exactly the work where a team wants genuine fluency rather than a one-off demonstration.

#### Approach

A monthly enablement programme across the whole firm, analyst to partner, running alongside a build track that turns the most repetitive, judgment-heavy reviews into supervised agents.

#### What we build

- Contract redlining agent Agent Extraction and comparison of lease and financing terms across documents, surfacing deviations for a human reviewer to rule on.

- IC memo interrogation agent Agent Adversarial stress-testing of investment-committee papers before presentation: the devil's advocate pattern, operationalised.

Capability 02

Portfolio operations

### Portfolio reporting, aggregated where founders already are.

#### Context

Funds with large portfolios collect reporting through whichever channel each founder prefers. Quarterly aggregation is manual, slow, and brittle.

#### Approach

An AI ingestion, normalization, and verification layer that meets founders in their existing channels, then reconciles everything into one consistent portfolio view, with the source for every figure preserved.

#### The point

No founder is asked to change how they report. The fund gets a single, verifiable picture of the portfolio, and the team's time moves from assembling the data to interrogating it.

Capability 03

Discovery & scoping

### Scoping across deal evaluation and memo workflows.

#### Context

Before any build, mapping where AI belongs across deal evaluation and investment-memo workflows, and, just as important, where it does not.

#### Approach

A scoping engagement: mapping the workflows worth automating, the judgment that must stay human, and the enablement the team needs to operate either way with confidence.

From Lisbon to London

### There is probably a workflow on your desk that fits.

If a recurring, judgment-heavy process comes to mind, that is usually the right place to start.

# About

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/about>

About Solven

## Finance-native and AI-native, in equal measure.

The firm

Solven Advisory is a boutique AI enablement and implementation consultancy, founded in Lisbon in 2025, working with private equity, real estate, and venture firms across Iberia and, increasingly, Europe.

The firm pairs operating-and-exit experience, built and scaled inside the consulting world, with hands-on AI delivery drawn from trading desks, investment research, and applied AI. That combination is deliberate. The people who decide where AI belongs in an investment firm should understand both the investment work and the technology underneath it.

We are thesis-driven. Everything we teach and build runs through a single idea, augmentation without cognitive atrophy, and a refusal to let capable people become editors of drafts they cannot defend. Solven is a member of the Anthropic Partner Network.

Where the team comes from

### The credibility is in the pedigree, not the pitch.

The team's backgrounds span institutional finance and applied AI. We let the experience speak plainly.

- TradingNon-linear and ETF trading desks at a global investment bank

- M&AMergers and acquisitions at corporate and investment banks

- InvestingSearch-fund analysis and venture-capital investing

- AI researchApplied AI research at national research institutes

- AI deliveryAgent development and AI strategy consulting

- TeachingAward-recognised teaching in programming and computer science

What we believe

### Three convictions that shape the work.

#### Judgment is the product.

In an investment firm, the deliverable is a defensible decision. AI should make that judgment sharper, never thinner.

#### Fluency is firm-wide.

From the newest analyst to the managing partner, everyone should know where Claude belongs in their own work.

#### The frontier is the job.

Staying current is not a one-off project. It is a standing discipline, which is why our work is monthly.

Talk to us

### We would rather have a conversation than send a brochure.

Tell us about your firm and where your team is today. We will be straight about whether we can help.

# Privacy

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/privacy>

Privacy

## Plain terms for personal data.

No marketing list, no advertising, and no cookie before you say yes. This page says what we do hold, why, and for how long.

This notice covers the personal data of people who visit this site, write to us, or book a call. It is written to be read, not scrolled past. Last updated 29 July 2026.

### Who we are

Solven Advisory is an AI enablement and implementation consultancy based in Lisbon, Portugal. For anything in this notice, the controller you are dealing with is Solven Advisory, and the fastest route is miguelmonteiro@solvenadvisory.ai.

### What we collect, and why

If you use the contact form, we receive the details you type: name, firm, email address, and your message. The form is delivered to our inbox by FormSubmit, a form-forwarding service; we use the details only to reply to you. If you book a call, scheduling runs on Cal.com's EU-hosted infrastructure, which collects the name, email address, and time slot you provide in order to place the meeting in both calendars. If you simply email or phone us, we hold the correspondence the way any firm holds its mail.

We run Vercel's cookieless analytics, which counts visits in aggregate, stores nothing on your device, and does not identify individuals. It runs whether or not you accept anything else. Video on the AI Flix page streams through YouTube's privacy-enhanced player, which stores nothing on your device until you choose to press play.

We would also like to understand how the site is actually read: which pages hold attention, where people stop, and which routes lead to a conversation. That requires cookies, so we ask before setting any. Nothing runs until you accept, declining takes a single click, and either choice is remembered. There is no advertising, no profiling for ad targeting, and no data sold or passed to brokers. There is no newsletter and no marketing list; when we say we reply to people, not leads, this notice is what that means in practice.

### The legal basis

We process contact and booking details because you asked us to: steps taken at your request before a possible contract (Article 6(1)(b) of the GDPR). We keep ordinary business correspondence on the basis of legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f)). Analytics cookies rest on consent alone (Article 6(1)(a), together with Article 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive as enacted in Portugal by Lei 41/2004). Consent is the entire basis there: withdraw it and the processing stops.

### Where the data sits

The site is hosted by Vercel. Form delivery passes through FormSubmit. Scheduling runs on Cal.com (EU infrastructure). Our email runs on Microsoft 365. If you accept analytics, PostHog processes that data on its EU cloud in Frankfurt, and Microsoft Clarity processes it under Microsoft's terms, which permit transfers outside the EU covered by the Standard Contractual Clauses. Each of these providers acts as a processor for the data described above; none of them is given your details for any purpose beyond delivering the service.

### How long we keep it

Correspondence is kept for as long as a working relationship, or the reasonable prospect of one, exists, and afterwards only as long as ordinary business record-keeping requires. If you would like something deleted sooner, ask.

### Your rights

You can ask for access to the data we hold about you, have it corrected or deleted, restrict or object to its processing, and receive a copy in a portable format. Write to miguelmonteiro@solvenadvisory.ai and we will deal with it directly. You also have the right to complain to the Portuguese supervisory authority, the CNPD, at cnpd.pt.

# Português

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/pt>

Formação e implementação de IA · Private Equity

## Implementação de IA para casas de investimento onde o critério é o produto.

Formamos equipas de investimento inteiras em IA e construímos sistemas sobre os fluxos de trabalho que realmente importam. A partir de Lisboa, para sociedades de private equity, imobiliário e venture capital.

A tese

O risco de um rollout de IA numa casa de investimento não é a adoção falhar. É o que acontece ao critério analítico quando a adoção resulta: analistas que se tornam editores de rascunhos que não conseguem defender em comité de investimento.

Todo o nosso trabalho é desenhado contra esse risco. O analista produz primeiro a sua análise; o modelo entra depois, como crítico, adversário e verificador, nunca como autor. Chamamos-lhe augmentation without cognitive atrophy: a IA torna o critério mais afiado, nunca mais fino.

O que fazemos

### Quatro práticas, quatro portas de entrada.

#### Programas de formação

Sessões práticas com Claude para toda a equipa, do analista ao managing partner, sobre os vossos próprios negócios, modelos e memorandos. Mensais, porque a fronteira é semanal.

#### Construção de sistemas

Agentes e automação sobre o trabalho real: revisão de contratos, interrogação adversarial de memorandos de comité de investimento, agregação de reporting de portefólio.

#### Due diligence de IA

Uma leitura independente sobre se a IA de uma empresa-alvo é capacidade genuína ou vocabulário de pitch, antes do term sheet e num formato defensável em comité.

#### Economia de tokens

Onde vai o orçamento de compute, o que devolve, e como fazê-lo durar o ano inteiro. O resultado é um P&L de tokens que os partners conseguem ler.

As sessões decorrem em português ou inglês, conforme a sala preferir. Os materiais escritos e o nosso journal são em inglês, porque as ferramentas e a fronteira o são.

Membro da Anthropic Partner Network

### Trinta minutos, com o escrutínio a correr na vossa direção.

Uma conversa com o Miguel, por vídeo ou telefone. Sem deck, sem sequência de follow-up, e com a resposta direta, incluindo «não somos a casa certa para isto».

# Português: Programas

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/pt/programas>

Formação · Os programas

## Fluência genuína em IA a todos os níveis da casa, do analista ao partner.

Sessões práticas com Claude que levam uma casa inteira dos primeiros princípios à construção com as ferramentas mais avançadas da suite.

Uma equipa formada uma vez é uma equipa a ficar para trás. A tecnologia por baixo deste trabalho muda a uma cadência semanal, pelo que uma casa que se formou há seis meses já está a operar sobre conhecimento desatualizado.

Os nossos programas são mensais precisamente porque a tecnologia é semanal. Cada pessoa aprende a reconhecer onde o Claude pertence no seu próprio trabalho, e mantém-se atual enquanto o mercado continua a mover-se.

Sempre na fronteira

### A fronteira move-se semanalmente. Mantemos a vossa equipa nela.

Novos modelos, ferramentas e capacidades chegam a uma cadência semanal. As nossas sessões chegam a um ritmo constante, para que a equipa nunca fique a mais de um passo da fronteira.

Como funciona

### Sobre os vossos fluxos de trabalho, não demonstrações genéricas.

- i Prática, sobre o trabalho real.As sessões correm sobre os negócios, modelos, memorandos e relatórios reais da casa, para que cada pessoa saia a saber onde o Claude encaixa no seu dia.

- ii O primeiro mês é amplitude.Orientação por toda a suite Claude, dos primeiros princípios à construção, para que toda a equipa partilhe um mapa do que é possível.

- iii A partir do segundo mês, aprofundamos.As sessões seguintes concentram-se nas áreas que a equipa considera mais valiosas. O arco da sessão mantém-se; o caminho adapta-se.

- iv Os formadores leem a sala.Os temas abaixo são orientação, não um guião. O ritmo e a ênfase seguem as pessoas na sala, do analista ao partner.

O que cobrimos

### A suite Claude completa.

Cada pessoa aprende que ferramenta serve que parte do seu trabalho, para que toda a suite esteja em jogo, não apenas a janela de chat.

#### Claude.ai

Pesquisa, redação e análise no browser, com Projects, ficheiros e pesquisa web num só lugar.

#### Claude Code

A ferramenta mais capaz da suite, e muito mais do que uma ferramenta para programadores: organizar ficheiros, automatizar trabalho recorrente, construir sistemas reais.

#### Claude for Chrome

O Claude a trabalhar ao lado das páginas e ferramentas que a vossa equipa já usa, sem sair do browser.

#### Claude Cowork

Um Claude que executa ações por todo o desktop, correndo um fluxo de trabalho de ponta a ponta em vez de apenas gerar texto.

#### Claude for Excel

Geração e auditoria de fórmulas, limpeza de dados e construção de modelos, com o Claude a raciocinar sobre o livro de Excel completo.

#### Claude for PowerPoint

Decks, gráficos e memorandos prontos para comité a partir de esboços, notas ou documentos de origem, alinhados com o formato da casa.

### O arco de quatro sessões.

De como um modelo realmente pensa, passando pela conversa e pela produção, até à construção de sistemas agênticos com Claude Code.

Primeira sessão · Fundamentos

#### Como a IA pensa.

Compreender o que um modelo está a fazer, o suficiente para saber quando confiar nele, e quando o contestar.

- A história da IA até ao avanço do transformer

- Tokens, embeddings, vetores e atenção

- Como funciona a geração: probabilidade, amostragem, variância entre execuções

- Onde o Claude é mais afiado, onde falha, e porque acontecem as alucinações

- O princípio do analista primeiro e o hábito da verificação

Como um modelo transforma texto em resultado

Segunda sessão · Conversa

#### Claude.ai.

O ofício de prompting que separa o resultado competente do convincente, e o padrão do advogado do diabo no seu centro.

- A interface: chat, Projects, Memory, ficheiros, pesquisa web, Artifacts

- Prompting estruturado: etiquetas XML, definição de papéis, especificações de resultado

- Few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought e metaprompting

- O padrão do advogado do diabo: o Claude como crítico, não como autor

- Gestão da janela de contexto, economia de tokens, saber quando parar

Anatomia de um prompt estruturado

Terceira sessão · Produção

#### O Claude nas ferramentas que já usam.

Onde os entregáveis da equipa realmente vivem: o livro de Excel, o deck e o desktop.

- Claude for Excel: geração de fórmulas, trilhos de auditoria, modelos financeiros, raciocínio entre folhas

- Claude for PowerPoint: decks a partir de esboços, alinhamento com a marca, memorandos prontos para comité

- Claude Cowork: automação no desktop e fluxos de trabalho entre aplicações

- A ideia maior: ferramentas e function calling

- Porque é que o Claude com ferramentas é fundamentalmente mais capaz do que o Claude sozinho

Ferramentas em torno do modelo

Quarta sessão · Construção

#### Construir com Claude Code.

A ferramenta mais capaz da suite, muito além de uma ferramenta para programadores: onde os fluxos de trabalho nativos de IA se acumulam mês após mês.

- O ciclo agêntico, prompts com controlo de versões e fluência em markdown

- Skills & SKILL.md: empacotar a especialidade da equipa como capacidade implementável

- MCP: ligar o Claude a bases de dados, APIs e sistemas internos

- O problema do horizonte infinito e condições de conclusão explícitas

- Padrões de automação: extração estruturada, processamento em lote, geração de relatórios

O ciclo agêntico

O fio condutor

### Cada sessão carrega o princípio do analista primeiro.

Os analistas produzem primeiro o trabalho formativo, e só depois trazem o Claude como crítico, red-teamer e verificador.

O risco de qualquer rollout é que pessoas talentosas se tornem editoras de rascunhos que não conseguem defender por inteiro. Desenhamos cada sessão ao contrário. Hábitos de verificação, o padrão do advogado do diabo, a IA como crítico e não como autora: as competências que o uso sem critério corrói são exatamente as que construímos.

É isso que queremos dizer com augmentation without cognitive atrophy, e atravessa as quatro sessões e tudo o que se segue a elas.

Estrutura do programa

### Construído para se ajustar à casa.

#### Mês a mês

Os programas são mensais e sem compromisso mínimo. Fiquem enquanto a fronteira continuar a mover-se, o que é o mesmo que dizer, enquanto for útil.

#### Sessões mais horas de construção

A formação combina-se com horas opcionais de construção e consultoria, para que a confiança ganha na sala se torne sistemas reais sobre fluxos de trabalho reais.

#### Presencial ou remoto

Nos vossos escritórios em Lisboa, remotamente, ou uma combinação. O formato segue a equipa, não o contrário.

#### Aberto a toda a casa

Do analista ao managing partner. A fluência é uma capacidade de toda a casa, não uma especialidade de poucos. Cada colaboração é dimensionada e orçamentada à medida.

### As perguntas que as casas fazem antes de marcar.

Respostas diretas às perguntas que normalmente antecedem a primeira chamada. O que ficar por responder aqui é uma boa abertura para a própria chamada.

**Q: Como é definido o preço?**

Cada colaboração é dimensionada e orçamentada individualmente: uma equipa de seis pessoas e uma casa com quarenta não são o mesmo programa. Os programas são mensais e sem compromisso mínimo, pelo que a decisão que estão a tomar é a de um mês, não a de um ano.

**Q: Quanto tempo da equipa exige o programa?**

O primeiro mês são quatro sessões que cobrem o arco completo, de como um modelo pensa até à construção com Claude Code. A partir do segundo mês, a cadência é mensal, aprofundando as áreas que a equipa considera mais valiosas. As sessões correm sobre os vossos próprios negócios, modelos e memorandos, pelo que o tempo é investido no trabalho real e não ao lado dele.

**Q: O que acontece aos dados da nossa casa durante as sessões?**

As sessões correm sobre os vossos negócios, modelos e memorandos reais, pelo que esta pergunta merece uma resposta precisa e não apenas tranquilizadora. O tratamento de dados é definido durante o scoping, antes de qualquer material ser aberto: por que contas passa o trabalho, em que termos, e o que é retido depois, se alguma coisa for. As respostas ficam por escrito antes da primeira sessão.

**Q: Em que ferramentas de IA formam, e estamos a prender-nos a um único fornecedor?**

Formamos na suite Claude: Claude.ai, Claude Code, e Claude no Excel, no PowerPoint, no Chrome e no Cowork. A Solven é membro da Anthropic Partner Network. É uma posição deliberada, não um acidente. Quanto ao lock-in: a primeira sessão ensina como funciona qualquer modelo de grande dimensão, dos tokens, atenção e probabilidade à origem das alucinações, e os hábitos de verificação que construímos são independentes do modelo. Se o mercado mudar, a fluência viaja com a vossa equipa.

**Q: As sessões são em português ou em inglês?**

Uma das duas, ou ambas. Estamos sediados em Lisboa e trabalhamos com casas de Lisboa a Londres, pelo que as sessões decorrem na língua que a sala preferir. Os materiais escritos são em inglês, porque as ferramentas e a fronteira o são.

**Q: Como sabemos que o programa resultou?**

Três formas que a casa pode ver em vez de aceitar de confiança. O próprio trabalho: resultados defensáveis em comité de investimento, com a contribuição humana legível para os revisores seniores. O P&L de tokens do nosso trabalho de economia de tokens: o que cada fluxo de trabalho custa e o que devolve, num formato que os partners conseguem ler. E as revisões de calibração integradas na metodologia, que detetam a deriva antes de ela se acumular.

**Q: Porquê a Solven e não uma grande consultora, ou fazer isto internamente?**

Três razões honestas. O trabalho é específico: fazemos uma coisa, para casas de investimento, e as sessões correm sobre os vossos negócios e memorandos, não sobre um currículo genérico. A cadência é o produto: a tecnologia muda semanalmente, e um projeto de formação pontual, interno ou externo, fica desatualizado num trimestre; a nossa colaboração é mensal porque a fronteira o é. E a tese é diferente: a maior parte da formação mede a adoção; nós desenhamos contra o offloading cognitivo, para que o critério fique mais afiado e não mais fino. Se o que uma casa precisa sobretudo é de gestão da mudança em mil postos, uma grande consultora é a escolha certa, e di-lo-emos.

**Q: O que acontece quando o programa termina?**

A colaboração é mensal e sem compromisso mínimo, pelo que terminar é uma decisão que podem tomar em qualquer mês. O que a casa guarda: os hábitos de verificação; os prompts e as skills construídos na quarta sessão, ficheiros com controlo de versões que vivem nos vossos sistemas; e tudo o que for produzido nas horas de construção. Nada está desenhado para tornar a saída difícil.

**Q: Isto vai tornar os nossos analistas dependentes da IA?**

Esse risco é a razão de a Solven existir. O modo de falha da maioria dos rollouts não é a adoção falhar; é os analistas tornarem-se editores de rascunhos que não conseguem defender. Cada sessão é construída ao contrário: o analista produz primeiro uma análise defensável, e só depois traz o Claude como crítico, red-teamer e verificador. Usado assim, o modelo afia exatamente as competências que o uso sem critério corrói. Chamamos-lhe augmentation without cognitive atrophy.

**Q: Os partners podem participar, ou isto é para analistas?**

A casa inteira, do analista ao managing partner. A fluência é uma capacidade de toda a casa, não uma especialidade de poucos, e cada sessão é ritmada para as pessoas na sala. As sessões dos partners são as que mais importam: a revisão liderada pelos seniores é o que sustenta a disciplina de verificação.

Membro da Anthropic Partner Network · Phase 1

Digam-nos onde a vossa equipa está hoje e como se desenha o próximo trimestre. Moldamos o arco à volta disso.

# Português: Abordagem

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/pt/abordagem>

A abordagem

## Augmentation without cognitive atrophy.

O risco na IA empresarial não é a adoção falhar. É o que acontece ao critério analítico quando a adoção resulta.

O risco

### Delegação cognitiva.

Quando um analista consegue produzir um rascunho polido num único prompt, o trabalho formativo deixa discretamente de acontecer: sentar-se com os dados, construir uma posição a partir de primeiros princípios, defender um número sob pressão.

O analista torna-se um editor passivo do output do modelo. Na página, a qualidade parece a mesma; por baixo, o critério vai-se adelgaçando. É contra este modo de falha que uma casa séria deve estar a desenhar.

O risco de qualquer rollout de IA é que pessoas talentosas se tornem editoras de rascunhos que não conseguem defender por inteiro.

O princípio

### IA como adversário, não como autor.

Tratamos o modelo como um testador do raciocínio do analista, não como um gerador desse raciocínio. O analista forma primeiro uma posição; o modelo desafia-a. O analista defende o trabalho; o modelo procura-lhe as fraquezas.

Usada assim, a IA afia precisamente as competências que o uso sem restrições corrói. O resultado é melhor e o critério por trás dele é mais forte, não mais fraco.

Os analistas produzem primeiro o trabalho formativo e só depois trazem o Claude como crítico, red-teamer e verificador.

A prática

### Restrições que aguentam sob pressão.

O princípio torna-se real na forma como o trabalho é sequenciado e revisto. A forma varia de casa para casa; a disciplina não.

- Analista primeiroO analista produz uma primeira versão defensável antes de recorrer ao modelo.

- Trabalho à vistaApêndices tornam a contribuição humana legível para os revisores seniores.

- VerificaçãoO padrão do advogado do diabo está integrado no fluxo de trabalho, não acrescentado no fim.

- CalibraçãoRevisões conduzidas por seniores detetam o desvio antes de ele se acumular pela equipa.

Uma tese, os dois lados do trabalho

### A abordagem governa como formamos e o que construímos.

Não é um diapositivo no início de um deck. É o princípio operativo por trás de cada sessão que damos e de cada sistema que entregamos.

#### Como formamos

Cada sessão é desenhada com o adversário primeiro, para que a equipa construa hábitos de verificação ao mesmo tempo que constrói fluência.

#### O que construímos

Agentes e fluxos de trabalho são desenhados para desafiar e verificar o raciocínio humano, nunca para o substituir em silêncio.

Ver na prática

### Os programas põem o princípio a trabalhar.

O arco de quatro sessões leva o princípio do analista primeiro desde os primeiros princípios até à construção com Claude Code.

# Português: Trabalho

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/pt/trabalho>

Trabalho selecionado

## Formação e construção, sobre fluxos de trabalho reais.

Um olhar sobre como os dois lados do trabalho se articulam nos fluxos que preenchem a semana de uma equipa de investimento.

Descrito pelo próprio trabalho, por fluxo e por estrutura, sem métricas que não possamos sustentar.

Capacidade 01

Due diligence · financiamento · comité de investimento

### Formação para toda a casa, com agentes sobre as revisões mais pesadas.

#### Contexto

Os fluxos de trabalho de due diligence, financiamento e comité de investimento são repetitivos e exigentes em critério: exatamente o trabalho em que uma equipa quer fluência genuína e não uma demonstração pontual.

#### Abordagem

Um programa mensal de formação para toda a casa, do analista ao partner, a correr em paralelo com uma linha de construção que transforma as revisões mais repetitivas e exigentes em critério em agentes supervisionados.

#### O que construímos

- Agente de revisão de contratos Agente Extração e comparação de termos de arrendamento e financiamento entre documentos, evidenciando desvios para um revisor humano decidir.

- Agente de interrogação de memorandos de CI Agente Teste adversarial dos memorandos de comité de investimento antes da apresentação: o padrão do advogado do diabo, operacionalizado.

Capacidade 02

Operações de portefólio

### Reporting de portefólio, agregado onde os fundadores já estão.

#### Contexto

Os fundos com portefólios grandes recolhem o reporting pelo canal que cada fundador prefere. A agregação trimestral é manual, lenta e frágil.

#### Abordagem

Uma camada de IA de ingestão, normalização e verificação que vai ao encontro dos fundadores nos canais que já usam, e depois reconcilia tudo numa visão de portefólio consistente, com a fonte de cada número preservada.

#### O essencial

A nenhum fundador se pede que mude a forma como reporta. O fundo fica com uma imagem única e verificável do portefólio, e o tempo da equipa passa de montar os dados a interrogá-los.

Capacidade 03

Descoberta & scoping

### Scoping sobre avaliação de negócios e fluxos de memorandos.

#### Contexto

Antes de qualquer construção, mapear onde a IA pertence nos fluxos de avaliação de negócios e de memorandos de investimento, e, tão importante quanto isso, onde não pertence.

#### Abordagem

Um trabalho de scoping: mapear os fluxos que vale a pena automatizar, o critério que tem de continuar humano, e a formação de que a equipa precisa para operar com confiança em qualquer dos casos.

De Lisboa a Londres

### Há provavelmente um fluxo de trabalho na vossa secretária que encaixa.

Se vos vier à cabeça um processo recorrente e exigente em critério, é normalmente aí que faz sentido começar.

# Português: Sobre

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/pt/sobre>

Sobre a Solven

## Nativa em finanças e nativa em IA, em igual medida.

A casa

A Solven Advisory é uma consultora boutique de formação e implementação de IA, fundada em Lisboa em 2025, que trabalha com casas de private equity, imobiliário e venture capital na Península Ibérica e, cada vez mais, na Europa.

A casa junta experiência de operação e de saída, construída e escalada dentro do mundo da consultoria, com implementação prática de IA vinda de mesas de trading, investigação em investimento e IA aplicada. Essa combinação é deliberada. Quem decide onde a IA pertence numa casa de investimento deve compreender tanto o trabalho de investimento como a tecnologia por baixo dele.

Somos guiados por uma tese. Tudo o que ensinamos e construímos passa por uma única ideia, augmentation without cognitive atrophy, e pela recusa de deixar pessoas capazes tornarem-se editoras de rascunhos que não conseguem defender. A Solven é membro da Anthropic Partner Network.

De onde vem a equipa

### A credibilidade está no percurso, não no pitch.

Os percursos da equipa atravessam a finança institucional e a IA aplicada. Deixamos a experiência falar com simplicidade.

- TradingMesas de trading não linear e de ETFs num banco de investimento global

- M&AFusões e aquisições em banca corporativa e de investimento

- InvestimentoAnálise em search funds e investimento em venture capital

- Investigação em IAInvestigação aplicada em IA em institutos nacionais de investigação

- Implementação de IADesenvolvimento de agentes e consultoria de estratégia de IA

- EnsinoEnsino premiado em programação e ciência da computação

Em que acreditamos

### Três convicções que moldam o trabalho.

#### O critério é o produto.

Numa casa de investimento, o que se entrega é uma decisão defensável. A IA deve tornar esse critério mais afiado, nunca mais fino.

#### A fluência é de toda a casa.

Do analista mais recente ao managing partner, todos devem saber onde o Claude pertence no seu próprio trabalho.

#### A fronteira é o trabalho.

Manter-se atual não é um projeto pontual. É uma disciplina permanente, e é por isso que o nosso trabalho é mensal.

Fale connosco

### Preferimos ter uma conversa a enviar uma brochura.

Falem-nos da vossa casa e de onde a vossa equipa está hoje. Seremos diretos sobre se podemos ajudar.

# Journal: Editors of drafts they cannot defend

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/blog/editors-of-drafts-they-cannot-defend>

Solven Journal · July 2026 · 4 min read

## Editors of drafts they cannot defend

The real failure mode of an AI rollout is not that analysts refuse the tools; it is that they end up polishing arguments they never built.

Every investment committee has a version of the same moment. A partner stops on a single figure, perhaps an exit multiple, a churn assumption, or a discount rate, and asks the analyst why it is what it is. The question is rarely about the number itself. It is a probe. If the analyst can walk backwards from that cell through the reasoning that produced it, the partner extends trust to the rest of the memo. If the analyst hesitates, the whole document is suddenly on the table.

That exchange only works if the person defending the work is the person who did it. This is precisely the assumption that careless AI adoption quietly breaks.

### The trap looks like productivity

When a model can produce a polished first draft of an IC memo in minutes, the rational-seeming move is to let it, and to spend the saved hours editing. The output improves. The pace improves. Everyone involved can point to something that looks like progress.

What has actually happened is the substitution of one cognitive act for a much weaker one. Producing an argument forces you to sit with the data, decide what matters, and commit to a position that could be wrong. Reviewing a plausible argument someone else produced demands far less, and it feels more complete than it is: a fluent draft reads as though the thinking has been done, so the reader's scepticism relaxes at exactly the moment it should sharpen. The analyst becomes an editor of a draft they cannot fully defend, and nothing on the page reveals it. Quality looks the same. The judgment underneath it thins out.

> There is a difference between owning an argument and having approved one, and an investment committee is designed to find it.

### Why investment work is exposed

Some professions can absorb this quietly. Investment work cannot, because its entire review structure presumes authorship. A memo passes from associate to principal to partner to committee, and at each stage the reviewer samples: they probe two or three load-bearing assumptions, watch how the author responds, and extend or withdraw trust accordingly. Sampling is efficient precisely because defending one number well is evidence that the author can defend the others.

Break the authorship assumption and the sampling breaks with it. The analyst who edited a generated draft may survive the first probe, because models are good at making assumptions sound reasoned, and fail the second, or survive both and carry an undetected error into a signed term sheet. The erosion also compounds. Analysts learn judgment by producing work and having it taken apart; the partners who take memos apart learned to do it by having their own taken apart. A firm that lets its juniors skip the production step is not saving time. It is quietly cancelling the apprenticeship that produces its future partners.

### Invert the workflow

The answer is not less AI. It is a different sequence. The analyst produces the first pass, the position, the numbers, and the reasoning, before the model sees any of it. Then the model is brought in as an adversary rather than an author: to attack the thesis, hunt for disconfirming evidence, stress the assumptions the analyst is most attached to, and check the arithmetic and the sourcing. We call this AI as adversary, not author, and it is the principle behind everything we do.

The inversion matters because the model is at its most valuable, and least corrosive, in the critic's chair. As an author it displaces the formative work; as an adversary it multiplies it. An analyst whose thesis has survived serious red-teaming walks into committee with better answers than either the unaided analyst or the prompt-and-polish one, and every answer is the analyst's own.

### What a firm can do about it

None of this survives on good intentions, because the prompt-and-polish route will always be faster on any given Tuesday. It has to be held in place by structure. Review norms can require that the human contribution be legible: a memo arrives with its formative work attached, and reviewers are entitled to ask which parts the analyst produced and which the model challenged. Partners can make provenance a normal question in committee, asked without ceremony, the way “why this number” is asked now. Senior-led calibration sessions surface drift in individual analysts before it compounds across the team: working a live deal problem together, unassisted first, then with the model as critic. And occasionally requiring a fully unassisted first pass does for the firm's bench what an audit does for its books: it verifies that the capability everyone assumes is there is actually still there.

Firms that get this right will be faster and sharper than the firms that merely adopted the tools, because they will have kept the one asset the tools cannot replace. The firms that get it wrong will not notice for a while; their documents will look excellent. Then one afternoon in committee a partner stops on a number and asks why, and nobody in the room owns the answer.

If that question is one your firm has started asking itself, we are glad to talk it through.

---

# Journal: How to tell whether the AI is real

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/blog/how-to-tell-whether-the-ai-is-real>

Solven Journal · July 2026 · 4 min read

## How to tell whether the AI is real

The questions that separate durable AI capability from rented capability, asked the way a deal team can actually ask them this quarter.

Most decks a deal team reads this year will describe the target as AI-powered. The phrase has stopped carrying information. It no longer distinguishes a company that has built something durable from a company that has an API key and a good copywriter, which means the work of distinguishing them has moved into diligence, where it belongs.

None of this requires a machine learning specialist on the deal team. It requires a handful of questions, asked in the right order and put to the right people, with as much attention to how the answers are given as to what they say.

> The question is not whether the target uses AI. It is what would remain if you removed everything the company rents.

### Start with where the model comes from

Ask the engineers, not the chief executive, and ask precisely. A "proprietary AI engine" in a deck very often means a rented frontier model with a carefully written prompt in front of it. That is not disqualifying; some of the best applied AI businesses are built on models anyone can rent. But it changes what you are pricing. You are no longer valuing a technology asset; you are valuing whatever has been built around a supplier.

The tell is precision. A strong team will describe its stack without hedging: which models, where fine-tuning ends and prompting begins, what was built and what was bought. A team that is vague about its own architecture either does not want you to know or does not know itself. Both answers are useful, and both should move the price.

### Then ask what sits around the model

In most AI businesses the durable asset is not the model at all. It is the data the company alone collects, and the depth to which the product is threaded into a customer's working day. So ask for those directly. What data do you hold that a well-funded competitor could not buy, license, or scrape within a year? What does the product learn from each customer's usage that makes it better for the next one? How long would it take a customer to leave, and what would they lose on the way out? None of these is a technical question. Each is an argument about the multiple, and each belongs in the investment committee discussion rather than in a technical annexe.

If the answers are thin, the AI can be entirely real and the business still replicable. Rented capability plus commodity data is a product, and possibly a good one, but it is not a moat, and it should not be priced as one.

### Ask what breaks when the supplier moves

A rented model is a supplier relationship, and model providers behave the way suppliers do: prices change, versions are retired, terms are rewritten. Ask which model versions the product depends on today. Ask what happened the last time one was deprecated, how long the migration took, and what it cost. A team that has switched providers once and can describe the exercise in detail has demonstrated something valuable. A team that has never considered the question is carrying a risk it has not priced, which means you would be.

The same part of the conversation should cover unit economics. Inference is a marginal cost that scales with usage in a way traditional software's costs never did. Ask what it costs to serve a customer, per seat, per transaction, per document, whatever the unit is, and which direction that number is moving. A gross margin that depends on model prices staying where they are, or on customers never using the product heavily, is not a margin; it is a hope. The encouraging sign is a team that knows its inference cost per unit without looking it up, because it watches the number weekly.

### Make them show rather than tell

Slides can claim anything. So ask for a live session, on inputs the deal team chooses, rather than a recorded demo built on inputs the company chose. Ask to see the evaluation suite, the tests that tell them whether a model update has quietly degraded the product, because a team without one is finding out from its customers. Ask what the last three months of engineering time actually went into; if the honest answer is prompts and interface work, the claimed depth of the AI intellectual property needs revising downwards. And ask who gets woken up when the model misbehaves in production, and what the runbook tells them to do.

None of this is hostile. Serious teams tend to enjoy these questions, because they finally get to talk about what they built. The teams that bristle are giving you information too.

### The short version

For a deal this quarter, the method compresses to five questions.

- Where, precisely, does the model come from?

- What do you hold that a competitor could not rent or buy?

- What happened the last time your model provider changed something, and what did it cost you?

- What does inference cost per customer, and which way is it moving?

- Show us, live, on inputs we choose.

Notice that none of these is exotic. They are supplier concentration, cost of goods, switching costs, and replicability. These are the questions investment committees have always asked, wearing new vocabulary. A deal team that asks them calmly will separate the targets that own their capability from the targets that rent it, and will price each accordingly. Expect that separation to be visible within the first meeting with the engineers.

If you would like a second pair of eyes on a live deal, we are happy to talk.

# Journal: Making every token earn its place

<https://solvenadvisory.ai/blog/making-every-token-earn-its-place>

Solven Journal · July 2026 · 4 min read

## Making every token earn its place

AI costs are metered and shaped by usage, which makes them easy to burn on low-value work; the remedy is a workflow-level P&L, not a bigger budget.

For two decades, software has been the best-behaved line in a firm's budget. A licence had a price, a seat count, and a renewal date. Finance could forecast the cost a year out and be right, because the cost had almost nothing to do with how much anyone used the product. The analyst who lived in the tool and the partner who opened it twice a quarter cost the firm exactly the same.

AI spend does not behave like this, and the difference is structural, not teething trouble. Frontier models are metered. Every request consumes tokens, every token is billed, and the invoice at the end of the month is a precise record of how the firm actually worked. The cost no longer follows headcount. It follows behaviour: the analyst mid-diligence and the partner who reads the finished memo no longer cost the firm the same.

That would be manageable if behaviour were disciplined by price at the point of use, but it is not. To the person typing, any single request feels free, because nothing about the moment of use signals otherwise. So usage flows towards whatever is easiest rather than whatever is worth the most. Entire data rooms are pasted into a context window when two documents would have answered the question. The most capable model is applied to formatting work a far smaller one handles. Ten drafts are requested where one would have been read. None of these decisions is careless on its own; in aggregate, they are the budget.

### Why budgets die in spring

The result is the pattern we built a practice around: a compute budget planned for the year that is substantially gone by the end of the first quarter. When it happens, firms tend to reach for one of two remedies, and both are wrong. Rationing access teaches the team that the tools are scarce, which quietly undoes the adoption the firm spent months building. Topping the budget up teaches the firm nothing at all, because next year's overrun is already in motion.

The real problem is neither the size of the budget nor the enthusiasm of the team. It is that nobody can say what the spend bought. An invoice denominated in tokens answers the question of how much with great precision while saying nothing about for what. No other line in the firm's accounts would survive that standard.

### The wrong unit

Tokens are the correct unit for billing and the wrong unit for management. A partner has no intuition for what a million tokens ought to cost or produce, and no dashboard will build one, because the unit does not map to anything the firm makes decisions about. What a partner can price instantly is work: a memo reviewed, a data room summarised, a board pack drafted, a screen of comparables assembled. Those are the units the firm already thinks in, negotiates in, and staffs against.

> A partner cannot price a token. Every partner can price a memo.

Workflow-level costing is the translation between the two. Instead of a single undifferentiated AI line, spend is attributed to named workflows, and each workflow acquires a unit cost: what first-pass diligence costs per target screened, what an adversarial review costs per investment committee memo, what a data room summary costs per room. Set beside the analyst-hours the work displaces or the speed it adds, each line supports an actual decision: keep, improve, or stop.

Attribution also changes what expensive means. A workflow with a high unit cost that saves a deal team two days per target is cheap. A workflow with a negligible unit cost that produces output nobody reads is pure waste, and there is more of the second kind than most firms expect, precisely because each instance is too small to notice. Without attribution, the worthless spend hides inside the aggregate, and the valuable spend gets caught in the same squeeze when the cuts eventually come.

### Measure, attribute, prune

The discipline itself is not complicated, though the order matters. Measurement comes first: usage made legible by team, by workflow, and by model, rather than arriving as one number on a monthly invoice. Attribution comes second, and it is the step firms skip: every token belongs to a named workflow, so the question in the budget review is never why AI is so expensive, but whether the memo-review workflow is worth what it costs. Pruning comes last, and it applies to workflows, not people. Some work moves to smaller models that produce the same output for a fraction of the spend. Some prompts get shorter and some context gets tighter. Some workflows are simply stopped, because a line that earns nothing should not survive the reading of the P&L that finally made it visible.

Pruning cuts in both directions, and this is the part an austerity-minded reader will miss. A workflow that clearly earns its cost should be fed, not rationed. Our view is that the honest outcome of the exercise is rarely a smaller budget; it is the same budget doing fewer things properly, paced so that it lasts the year it was planned for. The measure of success is not a lower invoice. It is a partner who can look at the invoice and explain it.

There is a reason this practice sits naturally beside our work on judgment. Cost discipline and analytical discipline are the same habit applied to different resources: knowing what a piece of work is for before commissioning it, and being able to defend it afterwards. A token P&L the partners can read is not a technical artefact; it is a governance document, and a firm where judgment is the product should insist on having one. If your firm's AI spend has become a number nobody can explain, we are glad to talk it through.
